name: Limewash
summary: Lime putty thinned with water to the consistency of milk and brushed onto a damp surface in several very thin coats. Each coat is semi-transparent while wet and dries many shades lighter, because the drying film fills with air and the calcium hydroxide carbonates to fine calcite. It is a matt, breathable, renewable skin over plaster, stone or brick; it wears by chalking and is renewed rather than repaired.

formation.how: Matured lime putty (calcium hydroxide) is diluted with water; pigments, when used, are pre-mixed in hot water. Additives such as tallow or linseed oil (for water shedding) or casein (for binding) may be included, tallow only during slaking. On the wall the film loses water and carbonates to calcite.

consistency.text: diluted to the consistency of milk
consistency.source: SPAB, Limewash (advice), https://www.spab.org.uk/advice/limewash; Bennett, B. (1997) Awash with Colour: The Decorative and Protective Roles of Limewash. tallowAddition.text: tallow can only be effectively included during the slaking process

carbonationConditions.text: carbonation is prolonged during periods of low temperature or high relative humidity

vapourPermeabilityRelativeToResinPaint.asReported: a vapour permeability of at least ten times that of modern resin paint
vapourPermeabilityRelativeToResinPaint.source: Hirst, E. (2002) Limewash and Distempers. The Building Conservation Directory, https://www.buildingconservation.com/articles/lwdistempers/lwdistempers.htm

constituents.role: organic binders that change water shedding and dusting

refractiveIndex.source: Anthony, J.W., Bideaux, R.A., Bladh, K.W. & Nichols, M.C. (eds.) Handbook of Mineralogy: Portlandite. Mineral Data Publishing, version 1 (2001-2005), http://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/portlandite.pdf

specularF0.derivation: normal-incidence Fresnel reflectance R0 = ((n-1)/(n+1))^2 over the carbonated film's calcite indices (1.486-1.658); the uncarbonated film (portlandite, 1.547-1.575) gives 0.046-0.050
specularF0.source: Born, M. & Wolf, E. (1999) Principles of Optics, 7th ed., Cambridge University Press, section 1.5; indices from Handbook of Mineralogy: Calcite and Portlandite, http://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/

dryingChange.text: semi-transparent when first applied, then dries to form an opaque coating; dries many shades lighter once applied; temporarily darkens after rain
dryingChange.source: Hirst, E. (2002), https://www.buildingconservation.com/articles/lwdistempers/lwdistempers.htm; Bennett, B. (1997), https://www.buildingconservation.com/articles/decorative-protective-limewash/decorative-protective-limewash.htm; SPAB, Limewash, https://www.spab.org.uk/advice/limewash

boundUpperCalcitePowder.note: fine white calcium carbonate powder; a carbonated limewash film is fine calcite and cannot exceed a clean fine calcite powder
boundUpperCalcitePowder.source: Omya Pars, Product Information OMYACARB 2-MH, edition 27/02/07, https://mychem.ir/uploads/tds/28825.pdf

optics.hiding: One coat does not hide the substrate: the film is thin and semi-transparent, so the ground shows through until several coats are built up; brush strokes and the substrate's texture stay visible.

matt.text: a simple type of matt paint made from lime and water

crazingWhenThick.text: crazing occurs when it is applied more liberally

acoustic.note: A thin film does not change the absorption of the surface it covers; use the substrate's record.

physicalMaterial.note: A skin over another substance: friction and footfall are the substrate's.

coats.asReported: at least three or four coats are usually needed

coatsMinimumTrade.asReported: a minimum of three coats should be applied for new work

renewalIntervalExternal.asReported: limewash typically requires renewing every five years

continuity.text: A continuous finish with no bays: it is worked across a whole face, coat by coat, each coat dried and the surface dampened before the next.

photograph: A dead-matt, slightly uneven white with a soft powdery bloom; brush marks and the texture of the ground show through.
Where it is thin or worn, the substrate glimmers through in patches; where it was laid thick, a fine craze.
Built-up layers soften arrises and fill fine detail over the years.
Outdoors, darker while wet after rain; chalking and streaking below ledges; indoors, greying on upward faces.
